text: Which one of the lanthanoids given below is the most stable in divalent form?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The stability of a divalent state can often be attributed to the stability of the electron configuration of that state. Among the options given, we can evaluate the electron configurations of each element in their divalent state to find out which is the most stable. The electronic configurations of the neutral atoms are :

Ce (Atomic Number 58) : $[Xe]4f^{1}5d^{1}6s^{2}$
Sm (Atomic Number 62) : $[Xe]4f^{6}6s^{2}$
Eu (Atomic Number 63) : $[Xe]4f^{7}6s^{2}$
Yb (Atomic Number 70) : $[Xe]4f^{14}6s^{2}$

In their divalent state (+2 oxidation state), the electron configurations would be :

Ce : $[Xe]4f^{1}5d^{1}$ (removal of the 2 electrons from the 6s orbital)
Sm : $[Xe]4f^{6}$ (removal of the 2 electrons from the 6s orbital)
Eu : $[Xe]4f^{7}$ (removal of the 2 electrons from the 6s orbital)
Yb : $[Xe]4f^{14}$ (removal of the 2 electrons from the 6s orbital)

Among these, Eu in its divalent state has a half-filled (4f) shell, which offers extra stability due to symmetrical electron distribution. Therefore, Eu (Atomic Number 63) is the most stable in the divalent form. 

So the correct answer is Option C : Eu (Atomic Number 63).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : [$Ni(CN)_{4}$]$^{2-}$ is square planar and diamagnetic complex, with dsp$^{2}$ hybridization for Ni but [$Ni(CO)_{4}$] is tetrahedral, paramagnetic and with $sp^{3}-$hybridization for Ni.

Statement  II : [NiCl$_{4}$]$^{2-}$ and [$Ni(CO)_{4}$] both have same d-electron configuration have same geometry and are paramagnetic.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is correct.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{8}$; strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ pairs the electrons and leaves one 3d orbital empty, giving $dsp^{2}$ hybridisation, a square planar shape and no unpaired electrons (diamagnetic).

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{4}]$: Ni(0) is $3d^{8}4s^{2}$; strong-field CO pairs all ten electrons into 3d ($3d^{10}$), giving $sp^{3}$ hybridisation, a tetrahedral shape and no unpaired electrons. It is diamagnetic, not paramagnetic, so Statement I is false.

$[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{8}$; weak-field $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ causes no pairing, giving $sp^{3}$ hybridisation, a tetrahedral shape and 2 unpaired electrons (paramagnetic).

$[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$ ($d^{8}$, paramagnetic) and $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{4}]$ ($d^{10}$, diamagnetic) share only the tetrahedral geometry, so Statement II is false.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Morning Shift

text:
Which of the following structures are aromatic in nature?


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A, the cyclopentadienyl anion, and B, the cycloheptatrienyl (tropylium) cation, are cyclic, planar and fully conjugated with $6π$ electrons $(4n+2,n=1)$, so both are aromatic.

C has four $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ bonds and no double bond at the ring fusion, so the two fusion carbons are $sp^{3}$ and break the cyclic conjugation; it is non-aromatic.

D, the cycloheptatrienyl anion, has $8π$ electrons $(4n)$ and is not aromatic.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Morning Shift

text:
The correct structure of product 'A' formed in the following reaction.

 
[IMG]
 

is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Benzaldehyde has no $α$-hydrogen, so in $\mathrm{NaOD}/\mathrm{D}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction.

$\mathrm{OD}{}^{-}$ adds to the carbonyl carbon of one molecule; the tetrahedral anion then transfers its aldehydic hydrogen, as hydride, to the carbonyl carbon of a second molecule and itself becomes the acid, which ends up as benzoate.


[IMG]

The hydride comes from the carbon of the first molecule, not from the solvent, so the new $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ group carries two H atoms (its own and the transferred one) and no deuterium.

The alkoxide $\mathrm{PhCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}^{-}$ takes $\mathrm{D}{}^{+}$ from the acid formed or from $\mathrm{D}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, giving $\mathrm{PhCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OD}$; deuterium on carbon (options C and D) or an $-\mathrm{OH}$ group (option B) cannot arise.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Morning Shift

text:
A 2.0 g sample containing MnO$_{2}$ is treated with HCl liberating $Cl_{2}$. The $Cl_{2}$ gas is passed into a solution of KI and 60.0 mL of $0.1 M Na_{2}S_{2}O_{3}$ is required to titrate the liberated iodine. The percentage of MnO$_{2}$ in the sample is $_____________. ($Nearest integer)

[Atomic masses (in u) Mn = 55; Cl = 35.5; O = 16, I = 127, Na = 23, K = 39, S = 32]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
First Step :

MnO$_{2} + 4$HCl $\to$ MnCl$_{2} + Cl_{2} + 2H_{2}O$

Here 1 mol of MnO$_{2}$ produce 1 mol of $Cl_{2}$

$\therefore$ Mole ratio of $n_{MnO_{2}}:n_{Cl_{2}}=1:1$

Second Step :

$Cl_{2} + 2KI$ $\to$ 2KCl $+ I_{2}$

Here, 1 mol of $Cl_{2}$ produce 1 mol of $I_{2}$

Mole ratio of $n_{Cl_{2}}:n_{I_{2}}=1:1$

Third Step :

$I_{2} + 2Na_{2}S_{2}O_{3}$ $\to$ 2NaI $+ Na_{2}S_{2}O_{3}$

1 mol of $I_{2}$ react with 2 mol of $Na_{2}S_{2}O_{3}$

Mole ratio of $n_{I_{2}}:n_{N_{2}S_{2}O_{3}}=1:2$

Given $Na_{2}S_{2}O_{3}$ is 60 mL of 0.1 M

$\therefore$ Number of moles of $Na_{2}S_{2}O_{3}$

= V (in L) $\times$ M (Molarity)

= $\frac{60}{1000}\times 0.1$

= 0.006 mol

$\therefore$ Number of moles of $I_{2}$

$=\frac{1}{2}(0.006)$

= 0.003

$\therefore$ Moles of MnO$_{2} = 0.003 ($as mole ratio of MnO$_{2}$ and $Cl_{2} = 1$ : 1)

Molar mass of MnO$_{2} = 55 + 32 = 87$

$\therefore$ Mass of MnO$_{2} = 0.003$ $\times$ 87 = 0.261 gm

Given MnO$_{2} = 2g$

$\therefore$ % of MnO$_{2} =$ $\frac{0.261}{2}\times 100=13%$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Morning Shift

If the work function of a metal is 6.63 $\times$ $10^{-19}J$, the maximum wavelength of the photon required to remove a photoelectron from the metal is $____________ nm. ($Nearest integer)

text: The vapour pressures of two volatile liquids A and B at 25${}^{\circ }$C are 50 Torr and 100 Torr, respectively. If the liquid mixture contains 0.3 mole fraction of A, then the mole fraction of liquid B in the vapour phase is $\frac{x}{17}$. The value of x is $______________$.

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{\mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{B}}}{1-\mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}^{\mathrm{o}}}{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}^{\mathrm{o}}}\left [\dfrac{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{B}}}{1-\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{B}}}\right ] \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{\mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{B}}}{1-\mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\dfrac{100}{50}\left [\dfrac{0.7}{0.3}\right ]=\dfrac{14}{3} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{B}}=\dfrac{14}{17} \end{array}$

text: The solubility product of a sparingly soluble salt $A_{2}X_{3}$ is 1.1 $\times$ $10^{-23}$. If specific conductance of the solution is 3 $\times$ $10^{-5} S m^{-1}$, the limiting molar conductivity of the solution is $x\times$ $10^{-3} S m^{2}$ mol$^{-1}$. The value of x is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $\mathrm{A}{}_{2}\mathrm{X}{}_{3}2\mathrm{A}{}^{3+}+3\mathrm{X}{}^{2-}$ with solubility $s$ (in $\text{mol L}^{-1}$):

$K_{sp}=(2s)^{2}(3s)^{3}=108s^{5}=1.1\times 10^{-23}$

$s^{5}\approx 1.0\times 10^{-25}\Rightarrow s\approx 1.0\times 10^{-5}\text{mol L}^{-1}=1.0\times 10^{-2}\text{mol m}^{-3}$

A saturated solution of a sparingly soluble salt is so dilute that its molar conductivity equals the limiting molar conductivity:

$\Lambda _{m}^{\circ }=\dfrac{κ}{c}=\dfrac{3\times 10^{-5}\text{S m}^{-1}}{1.0\times 10^{-2}\text{mol m}^{-3}}=3\times 10^{-3}\text{S m}^{2}\text{mol}^{-1}$

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Morning Shift

text:
For a first order reaction A $\to$ B, the rate constant, k = 5.5 $\times$ $10^{-14} s^{-1}$. The time required for 67% completion of reaction is x $\times$ $10^{-1}$ times the half life of reaction. The value of x is $_____________ ($Nearest integer)

(Given : log 3 = 0.4771)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \because \mathrm{kt}=\ln \dfrac{\mathrm{A}_{0}}{\mathrm{A}} \\  \\ \dfrac{\ln 2}{\mathrm{t}_{\frac{1}{2}}}\mathrm{t}_{67%}=\ln \dfrac{\mathrm{A}_{0}}{0.33\mathrm{A}_{0}} \\  \\ \dfrac{\log 2}{\mathrm{t}_{\frac{1}{2}}}\mathrm{t}_{67%}=\log \dfrac{1}{0.33} \\  \\ \mathrm{t}_{67%}=1.566\mathrm{t}_{1/2} \\  \\ \mathrm{x}=15.66 \end{array}$

Nearest integer $=16$

text: Number of complexes which will exhibit synergic bonding amongst, $[Cr(CO)_{6}]$, $[Mn(CO)_{5}]$ and $[Mn_{2}(CO)_{10}]$ is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Synergic bonding in a metal carbonyl is $σ$ donation from the lone pair on the carbon of CO into a vacant metal orbital together with $π$ back donation from a filled metal d orbital into the vacant $π^{\ast }$ orbital of CO; each bond strengthens the other.

$[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{6}]$, $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{5}]$ and $[\mathrm{Mn}{}_{2}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{10}]$ all contain metal-CO bonds with the metal in the zero oxidation state, so each metal has filled d orbitals for back donation and each complex shows synergic bonding.

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Morning Shift

text:

$\therefore 0.4\mathrm{g}\mathrm{AgBr}=\frac{80}{188}\times 0.4$

$%$ of $\mathrm{Br}$ in given organic compound
